# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Linux Shell Executing Decoded Base64 or Code From a Temporary Directory** · `T1059.004_linux_suspicious_shell_execution` · [T1059.004](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1059.004_linux_suspicious_shell_execution for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     Image=<value>  CommandLine=<value>
Checked:      1. Decode the Base64 blob or read the script or binary in the temporary directory -> <result>
              2. Identify the parent chain - an SSH session, a web server, cron, a container entry point -> <result>
              3. Check for network connections and new files from the same process tree -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | package_manager_helpers (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Installers and package builds that unpack helpers into /tmp and run them
- Provisioning scripts that pass small Base64 payloads to a shell

Never tune:
- Never filter Base64 piped into a shell by user or host - the pattern has no routine administrative use.
- Never filter binaries in /dev/shm.

## Escalation to incident response

```text
Alert:        T1059.004_linux_suspicious_shell_execution for <host> at <time, UTC>
Escalated:    <the condition met, from the list below>
Observed:     Image=<value>  CommandLine=<value>
Who / where:  <account> on <host>; source <host or address, if any>
Risk:         base 60 + <conditions met> = <score>
Preserved:    Process creation with the full command line and parent chain -> <where it is saved>
              The decoded content or the file in the temporary directory, with its hash -> <where it is saved>
              Network connections of the process tree -> <where it is saved>
Containment:  none yet | <action taken, time UTC>
Recommended:  Contain the account or service that ran the code, isolate the host if a payload ran, and hunt for the same blob or file name on other hosts
```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. The decoded text or script downloads, opens a network connection or changes persistence
2. The parent is a web server or another service account
3. The binary in the temporary directory is unknown to the host

Risk conditions: user is privileged +15 · host is critical +15 · outside business hours +10 · known vendor software -25 · approved change window -15.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Kill the process tree after saving its details
2. Lock the account or stop the service that started it
3. Isolate the host if a payload ran
